tasks.title: tools/balance.mjs --siege -n 400 — flag any card above 65% or below 40% round win rate at parity; report the win-condition distribution
tasks.note: Built, not merely run — the arg parser accepted only --campaign, so the gate command named in three places had never been able to execute. Two sweeps: mirrored card-at-parity with the draft disabled, and a full-rules natural sweep for the win-condition rule. n=400 parity matches (1702 rounds) + 100 natural (416). Null control P1 50.0% with both legs in band, 25/25 cards exercised, King-pop share 90.1% against the 70% points ceiling. Proven able to fail in both directions and deterministic across three runs (7bb44a43 pre-instrumentation). Reports 4/25 cards out of band, which is the gate working.

tasks.title: P7 gate — balance --siege green, mp-smoke through a full best-of-five, all prior suites, commit
tasks.note: Every other clause is green: mp-smoke, audit-test (three runs), test:siege 45/45 three times, npm test 40/40, editor-test, siege-test 25/25, playtest --all 774 shots, four-engine determinism at sim digest 2856ed88, campaign 52/52 at an unchanged output hash. The gate clause "balance --siege green" is not, and deliberately so: airlift measures 81.4% [69.6%, 89.3%] at parity against a 65% ceiling. Closing P7 needs either a data.js rebalance or an amendment to how the gate reads tier-3 cards. See knownIssues.

openRisks: RESOLVED 2026-08-22: cross-engine float determinism holds with the FULL solver. V8, SpiderMonkey and JavaScriptCore produce bit-identical digests over 1800 steps with SAT, manifolds, warm starting, impulses, position solve and sleeping all active. The relay audit model in ARCHITECTURE.md section 5 is viable and the lenient fallback is not needed. Re-run with `npm run test:determinism:all` after any change to physics.js or sim.js (podman; WebKit cannot launch on this host directly).
52 authored campaign levels is the largest single time cost in the plan and depends on the editor being pleasant to use, which is why P4 precedes P5.
Simultaneous siege means the loser watches their own fortress fall in a 260x150 window. If that reads as noise rather than tension the mode's core hook fails, and it cannot be evaluated before P6.
The trajectory preview dots are drawn very faint against the sage hills and are hard to read while aiming. Cosmetic, deferred from P2.

RESOLVED 2026-09-01: the airlift + gale + bedrock defensive lock was never confirmed, because the harness measured airlift ALONE at 87.3% before any combination was tried. DESIGN made mutual exclusion in the draw conditional on the harness confirming a lock, so that precondition was never met and exclusion is not the applicable fix. Airlift alone is the finding.
balanceNotes: P3.7 tap-timing sweep, winning timings (tap beats no tap) out of ~47: spike 47, hulk 46, pebble 32, wedge 20, boomer 10, chip 5, zip 5, lob 2. Lob's 2/46 was a design fault and is being fixed (tap was only legal in the flying phase, so a bomb could not be detonated after landing; adding rest-phase tap plus a fuse). Chip and Zip at 5/47 are being left alone deliberately: both must be triggered at a particular distance to work - split too early and the fragments fan wide of the target, too late and it has already hit - which is genuine skill expression rather than a reflex test, and it is how the equivalent abilities behave in the games this borrows from. Revisit with tools/balance.mjs in P7 using human play data rather than a fixed draw vector; a narrow window against ONE scripted shot is not the same as a narrow window in play.

knownIssues: SIEGE (solo) plays end to end, and now with its own budget and cards: a second review of abfd28f found that openEditor built the correct Siege draft from siegeBudget and the held cards and then unconditionally rebuilt it plain seven lines later, so the build phase never actually saw either. Fixed at the source in game.js, along with a second, previously-dormant bug the fix would otherwise have exposed (a card's budget bonus composing twice on every blueprint reload). A full best-of-five runs through the UI - build, lock-in, simultaneous assault, corner preview, round resolution, draft, standings, match end and replay - and is asserted by `npm run test:siege` (tools/siege-match.mjs, 45 assertions in Chromium, seed pinned so the scoreline and assertion count are identical run to run). Write-up in docs/WORKLOG.md under 'Defect 1 and its knock-on effects', which also corrects two claims the P7.6/P7.7 write-up got wrong.
SIEGE (online) has no UI at all. worker.js, net.js and relay-audit.js are built, deployed and tested, but nothing in the client connects to them.

The bot loses most rounds against a fortress it cannot out-shoot. tools/siege-match.mjs finished 3-1 and 3-0 on consecutive runs against a deliberately cheap blueprint - observed before its match seed was pinned on 2026-09-01, so no longer reproducible from that tool by re-running it, but the finding itself stands. That is a balance question for P7.8, not a defect, but the difficulty of the ballistic aimer at 0.82 has never been measured against a human.

tools/siege-match.mjs is deterministic across eight consecutive runs (45/45 assertions, scoreline You 3 - 2 Bot every time, some under concurrent CPU load), but one race remains by design rather than by proof: the bot's shot cadence is scheduled off wall-clock performance.now() via siege.botNextShot, not off sim ticks. A sufficiently loaded machine is therefore still a plausible source of scoreline variance. Unobserved so far. The honest fix is to schedule the bot off the fixed step; it was left alone deliberately because it is a change to game behaviour rather than to the gate.

game.js parses ?siege-seed= unconditionally rather than behind ?smoke-test, following the existing ?ammo= precedent. Harmless for solo Siege, where nothing is at stake in the seed. It must NOT reach online Siege: DESIGN.md gives the relay ownership of the match seed, so a client-supplied override there would let a player choose their own draft offers. Check this when the online Siege UI is wired up.

AIRLIFT is a confirmed balance outlier at parity and untouched: 85.7% with the harness default, 81.4% [69.6%, 89.3%] with --no-lane-respend, against a 40-65% band. Two harness artefacts were found and removed first - the bot did not know to pop an invulnerability shield (1.6 points, fixed in 712bb39) and buildFortress respent the scrap freed by airlift's flight lane (4.3 points). Roughly 16 points above the ceiling remain and belong to the card. The lever is NOT lift, driftRange or balloonHp: the balloon already dies on shot 1 in 120/120 rounds, the King dies 100% of the time with or without the card (mean 1.65 vs 1.95 shots), and under --no-lane-respend the holder already spends 109 fortress scrap against the opponent's 145. The only remaining lever is the total damage immunity, which is the card's printed text and identity, and DESIGN warns against nerfing it into pointlessness. Not changed - this is a game-design decision, not a defect fix.

THE 40/65 BAND AND TIER 3 CONFLICT, and airlift is where it bites. CARD_TIER_RULES makes tier 3 drawable only at deficit exactly 2, so a Desperado card can only ever be held by a player two rounds down who needs three straight wins. The parity sweep holds budgets, round index and deficit equal by definition, so it measures tier-3 cards in a state where they cannot be drawn. DESIGN says the 40-65 band applies to Desperado cards AND that the guard against a runaway is the draw restriction; those two statements cannot both govern tier 3. At 81.4% per round, airlift converts to roughly 0.814^3 = 53% for the three consecutive wins its holder actually needs, which is arguably the intended function of a Desperado card. The measurement that would settle it is a per-card MATCH comeback rate from the natural sweep at the real deficit, not a per-round rate at parity. Until that exists, treat airlift's flag as well-measured but not yet actionable.

THREE OF THE FOUR FLAGGED CARDS ARE INSIDE THE NOISE and unresolved: gale 69.7% [57.8%, 79.4%], iron-ration 37.3% [26.7%, 49.3%], kingslayer 33.3% [22.9%, 45.6%]. At 55-70 rounds per card the intervals straddle their thresholds, so tuning them on these numbers would be fitting to sampling error. Resolving them means a higher -n: -n 400 gives about +/-12% per card and takes 8 minutes, so -n 2000 for roughly +/-5.5% costs about 40 minutes. Do that before treating any of the three as a real outlier.

check.mjs does not enforce line budgets for anything under tools/. Its budget loop iterates plan.modules only and never plan.tools, so the budget on any tools/ entry in docs/FILE-PLAN.json - including the ones raised deliberately for tools/balance.mjs - is documentation kept honest by hand rather than a gate. tools/balance.mjs is currently 1138 lines against a documented 1250.
